title: How Astronauts Live
subtitle: Sleep, food and toilets
yt_title: How Do Astronauts Go to the Bathroom? 🚽 | Ep. 124 #shorts
description:
Episode 124 of a daily journey through the universe. 🚽
We move into the space station: sleeping in a sleeping bag tied to the wall, about 16 sunrises a day, food in pouches and tortillas instead of bread, a toilet that uses air instead of gravity, and recycling sweat and urine into drinking water.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 125: Next stop, spacesuits. A spacecraft shaped like a person.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

Images: NASA (public domain)
Narration: AI voice

#space #astronaut #astronomy #shorts #science #nasa

segments.text: Episode one hundred and twenty-four. Next stop... how astronauts live.
In space, there's no up or down. So astronauts sleep in sleeping bags tied to the wall, so they don't float into things.
segments.headline: Sleeping on the wall

segments.text: The station circles Earth about sixteen times a day. That's sixteen sunrises, so they use eye masks.
Food comes in pouches and cans. Crumbs could float into eyes and equipment, so they eat tortillas instead of bread.
segments.headline: Tortillas, not bread

segments.text: Without gravity, fluid moves up into the head. Food tastes bland, so astronauts love hot sauce.
segments.headline: Bring the hot sauce

segments.text: And the toilet? It uses air flow instead of gravity, like a gentle vacuum cleaner, pulling waste away.
segments.headline: A vacuum toilet

segments.text: Then the station recycles water from sweat and urine, and turns it back into clean drinking water. About ninety-eight percent of it.
To keep their bones and muscles strong, astronauts exercise about two hours every day.
segments.headline: 2 hours of exercise daily

segments.text: And when they get home, many find it hard to walk at first. Their bodies forgot gravity.
segments.headline: Relearning gravity

segments.text: Tomorrow, the suit that keeps an astronaut alive outside. A personal spacecraft, shaped like a person. Follow, so you don't miss episode one hundred and twenty-five.
